chunks: And from him (Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad) from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a person in Ihram who caught game: does the person who enters Ihram (Al-Muhill) eat from it? He said, 'There is no obligation on the Al-Muhill; rather, the ransom (Fidya) is upon the Al-Muhrim.'

key_terms.الْمُحِلُّ: The one who enters Ihram (or the one who is not currently in Ihram, depending on context of 'catching')
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Who bears the ransom (Fidya) when a person in Ihram catches game, and can the one who enters Ihram eat it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the permissibility of consuming the game for the one who lifts the Ihram restrictions (Al-Muhill) is independent of the penalty incurred by the one who was in Ihram (Al-Muhrim). This ruling underscores the principle that the *Fidya* (ransom) is a personal obligation tied to the state of the pilgrim at the time of the act, rather than a condition for the validity of the catch itself for others. It highlights the distinct legal statuses of the *Muhrim* and *Muhill* in the jurisprudence of Hajj and Umrah.
